title: Words Speak Louder Than Code: Investigating Cognitive Heuristics in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Detection
abstract: arXiv:2606.30587v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Researchers and practitioners increasingly apply Large Language Models (LLMs) for automated vulnerability detection. Recent work has shown that LLMs are susceptible to the same cognitive heuristics that bias human judgment. Yet, no work has investigated whether these heuristics affect a model's assessment of code vulnerabilities. In this paper, we present the first systematic exploration of cognitive heuristics in LLM-driven code vulnerability detection. We introduce a controlled framework that holds the code fixed and only varies the surrounding context to trigger three cognitive heuristics: the halo effect through author attribution, the framing effect through task objectives and consequences, and the anchoring effect through prior analysis results. Within this framework, we evaluate eight LLMs across three programming languages. Our results demonstrate that all evaluated models are susceptible to these heuristics. Cross-mode

translated_title: 言语胜过代码：研究基于大语言模型的代码漏洞检测中的认知启发式
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.30587v2 公告类型： replace-cross 摘要：研究人员和从业者越来越多地将大语言模型（LLM）应用于自动化漏洞检测。最近的研究表明，大语言模型容易受到与影响人类判断相同的认知启发式偏差的影响。然而，目前尚无研究探讨这些启发式是否会影响模型对代码漏洞的评估。在本文中，我们首次对大语言模型驱动的代码漏洞检测中的认知启发式进行了系统性探索。我们引入了一个受控框架，该框架保持代码本身不变，仅改变周围的上下文信息，以触发三种认知启发式：通过作者署名触发的晕轮效应、通过任务目标和后果触发的框架效应，以及通过先前分析结果触发的锚定效应。在该框架下，我们评估了八种大语言模型在三种编程语言上的表现。我们的结果表明，所有被评估的模型都容易受到这些认知启发式的影响。跨模型（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究首次系统性地发现，大语言模型在代码漏洞检测中会受到晕轮效应、框架效应和锚定效应等认知启发式的影响——即使代码本身保持不变，仅仅改变其周围的上下文信息（如作者署名、任务目标、先前分析结果）就足以左右模型的漏洞判断。
en_tdlr: This first systematic study reveals that LLMs are susceptible to cognitive heuristics—the halo effect, framing effect, and anchoring effect—in code vulnerability detection, showing that merely varying the surrounding context while keeping the code fixed can sway the models' vulnerability assessments.
